subject: Urgent: Marigold Health private cluster — sudden throughput collapse & error surge
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@marigold.health>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vikram.patel@marigold.health, megan.ross@marigold.health
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact — private cluster throughput collapse

Marissa,

We started seeing an abrupt drop in inference throughput on our private VPC cluster at ~08:50 PDT. Concurrently, our service dashboard shows a spike in 502/504 and a 4x jump in tail latency for patient-facing requests. This is across all regions served by the cluster (only US for us).

We exported the runtime logs and attached a short snapshot (marigold_error_snapshot.png); full logs are in the tar. We also see unusual KV cache growth in the runtime metrics (cache size keeps growing and GC isn't reclaiming as expected). Paging our NOC now but wanted Redwood involved given this is impacting live clinical triage flows.

Impact: degraded user experiences across ~25% of requests, several partner integrations timing out. We need immediate mitigation and an executive-level update if this cannot be resolved in the hour.

Please advise next steps and who from Redwood is available for an urgent sync.

—Priya
Director, Platform Operations
Marigold Health
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@marigold.health>, vikram.patel@marigold.health
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — private cluster throughput collapse

Priya — thanks for the heads up and for sending the logs. I'm on the call with SRE now and we want to run a few quick, low-risk mitigations while we triage:

- Switch incoming traffic to the secondary read path (we can route by prefix) to reduce burst pressure — 2–3 minute change.
- Apply a temporary KV cache cap to stop unbounded growth (runtime flag) — non-disruptive to correctness, reduces memory pressure.
- If errors persist, fall back to the last-known-good model shard replica (we have a warm copy from last week).

Can you confirm whether you have an open maintenance window for a 5–10 minute traffic reroute now? If not, we'll coordinate a canary that targets 10% of traffic first.

I'll get SRE and our on-call kernel team on a triage bridge; copying Laura for exec coordination and Jonas for runtime kernel knobs. Aditya — can you be ready to prepare an exec summary and potential credit proposal if this looks like a prolonged SLA impact?

—Marissa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Marigold private cluster — initial triage notes and ask

Team — quick internal notes from the triage bridge (joined with Priya/Vikram/Megan):

- Symptoms: sudden p95/p99 latency increases and 502/504s starting 08:50 PDT. Metrics show increased decoder CPU wait and a growing KV cache footprint on shard group 3.
- Hypothesis: a model-serving kernel path regressed under a specific token distribution from Marigold’s production prompt set; combined with a recent tenant metadata change that increased prefix size, caused cache thrash.
- Immediate mitigations applied: traffic split to secondary read path (10% -> 100% staged), KV cache cap (runtime flag), and we restored a previous model shard replica for the most impacted host group. Initial observations: error rate dropped ~40% within 8 minutes, tail latency p99 improved ~25% but p95 still elevated.

Ask / next steps:
1) Jonas — run a kernel parameter rollback and gather perf counters from the restored replica (priority).
2) SRE — run targeted GC and confirm whether any OOM/restart loops are pending; preserve core dumps if they occur.
3) Aditya — draft a one-page exec summary (impact, timeline, mitigations, ask) and prepare two remediation options with estimated customer credits.
4) Laura — advise on whether this rises to VP/CEO notification (customer is hitting triage workflows).

Attachments: thread_logs_20280710.tar.gz (from customer), short snapshot provided by Priya.

I'll keep the bridge open until we have a firm remediation.

—Marissa
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <priya.shah@marigold.health>, vikram.patel@marigold.health
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — private cluster throughput collapse

Priya / Vikram — thank you for your patience and for working with the triage team this morning. Brief exec update below to share with internal leadership at Marigold: 

Summary (what happened): your private VPC experienced a cascade where decoder wait and increased prefix sizes triggered KV cache amplification on a subset of shard group 3; a recent minor metadata change increased average prefix length which exposed a kernel path regression.

What we did (what you should see now):
- Applied temporary KV cap and GC pressure adjustments; removed the regressed kernel path by rolling back the kernel param; restored traffic to primary read path in a staged canary.
- Error rate reduced by ~75% vs peak; overall p95 latency remains ~12% above baseline but trending down. No additional OOMs observed after GC.

What we recommend next (24–72h):
1) We propose a targeted kernel patch that avoids the pathological allocation pattern — Jonas will own the patch and run overnight tests on a private replica.
2) Longer-term: adjust your prefix tokenization config to reduce average prefix length and adopt a cache-bounding policy; we will provide suggested config changes and a rollout plan.
3) Operational: request an on-prem SRE runbook addendum (we'll draft) and 3 months of extended monitoring retention for the hot keys.

Commercial / exec ask: in recognition of the customer impact, Redwood recommends a one-time credit for the affected service period. Aditya will follow up with a proposed credit band and formal wording for customer acceptance.

I'll set a 30-minute exec sync for later today to review the remediation plan and confirm the credit proposal. Marissa — please share the one-pager and any customer message drafts.

—Laura
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
